miscText: With Tui’s Garden, ambient and folktronica slowly morph into a mesmerizing IDM trance.
author: Indiemusic

miscText: With Taihua, Benjamin Gibert brings together IDM, field recording and folktronica, crafting a work that is both beautiful and demanding, where technical inventiveness is placed at the service of a deep and sincere rootedness in nature.
author: Indiemusic

miscText: Finding one’s rightful place and weaving affinities with the environment through creation... that, to me, is ecology.

We were asked to take off our shoes as soon as we arrived. We did everything barefoot — hiking, grocery shopping, visiting our neighbors, exploring. That experience deeply influenced the creation of the album. It’s a very simple thing, but it stayed with me throughout, almost obsessively, because it’s not something I’m used to. I decided to open the record with a barefoot track, like an entry ritual without shoes.
I set myself the rule of collecting and working with the most endemic sounds possible in the places I passed through, listening with a traveler’s ear, in a constant state of wonder.

Taihua is a tale — an immersive narrative, the story of a traveler who eventually dissolves into the environment they journeyed through. I wanted the listener to let themselves be guided, to discover, to adapt, and to remain in a state of non-mastery. For the artwork, I wanted to stage this barefoot wanderer, splashed and then submerged by sea foam, on the verge of merging with their environment.
I think that, deep down, this wanderer has become a silky wave, spending its life lapping at the coastal forest.
